title: Pad Node_Select mirror re-implements click_select's selection rule instead of sharing it
detail: The junction→select / else→clear rule is now written twice (click_select at exec.odin:409-412 and the mirror at :195-200). The mirror's own comment names click_select's rule. A rule change must be made in two places, and the codebase's own discipline is ONE copy.
recommended_fix: Extract a shared select_node(inp, id) helper (junction→select, else→clear both) and call it from click_select's junction branch and the Node_Select mirror, so one copy owns the selection rule.

title: Dpad mirror unconditionally clears a mouse/touch pipe selection on any pad step (mixed input)
detail: sel_pipe is one shared Input field; the mirror writes sel_pipe=-1 on every Node_Select (both branches). In the live app (dispatch_frame runs mouse then controller maps on the same Input), a mouse-selected pipe — QoS panel/popover open — is silently deselected by the first dpad nudge, against the 'all inputs additive' doctrine.
recommended_fix: Leave a mouse/touch pipe selection intact when the pad cursor lands on a terminal (the pad owns no pipe selection to clear), or track which device owns the selection and only mirror over same-owner selections.

title: ui_hook wiring by scenario-name string matching grows to three names in a scattered chain
detail: Hook selection is keyed on scenario-name strings in run_input_parity, and check_states separately name-switches the state assertions; each UI-wired scenario touches three scattered sites. A rename silently re-wires the scenario (drops the hook), and for esc_ui the negative pin goes weak without failing.
recommended_fix: Add a declarative field to Parity_Scenario (e.g. ui_hook: bool or a hook enum) set at the scenario site; run_input_parity and check_states read the field instead of matching name strings.

title: Harness pipe_demolish_btn_center hand-computes the pipe midpoint the same diff just single-sourced
detail: The N2-r4 fold centralizes the anchor in render (render draw + input hit-test), yet the new test helper re-derives the midpoint from fixture constants — a third copy of the formula. Drift fails loudly (press misses the button, expected command mismatch), so this is maintainability debt, not a correctness bug.
recommended_fix: Plumb the fixture topology into build_scenarios (the fixture is built per-run in drive_parity; hoist it) so pipe_demolish_btn_center delegates to rnd.pipe_anchor, matching the hit-test it must stay aligned with.
